F7a (mips.c:4680 emits GP saves high-to-low unconditionally; a real incoming-arg WAR anti-dependence does not reorder them — s8). F7b (an empty beqz delay slot needs a block with no eligible single insn while the target's holds four — s6). The s7 residual table accounts for 13/13 with nothing left over. The canonical-asm endgame gate is a MEASURED FAILED gate (scan_hand_coded tier LOW, 0/8, for this function and its sibling — s6) and no coercion/spelling family has an in-hand SOTN-master precedent.

frontier.mechanism: Depth 2 on the goto-loop chassis is now the measured minimum, down from depth 3, and it is minimal across five idioms and both declaration orders. The binding constraint is arithmetic: with p assigned first (required for the target's materialisation order) count sits at 5 raw refs / live_length 7 = 14285 and p at 5/8 = 12500, so p needs 6 weighted references. Deleting a count reference is only possible by deleting the outer guard the target has, which costs a point (14).
frontier.next_probe: Only worth time if a session is preparing a submission, which cannot happen while H1 stands. The single untried direction is unchanged from s8: lengthen count's live range WITHOUT adding a count reference — an intervening real computation the target also performs — and the target performs none. Success criterion is score 13 at wrap depth <= 1, not a lower score.

frontier.hypothesis: F12 (new, and deliberately narrow) — the loop-note surface itself is a lever nobody had varied before s9, so other real C control-flow constructs may change flow.c's raw-vs-weighted reference accounting in ways the do-while/while/goto trio did not.
frontier.mechanism: s9 showed that swapping the walk's loop construct (do-while / while / tail-tested goto / top-tested goto) changes the WEIGHTING of every reference in the function, not just the loop's own, and moved the required device from depth 3 to depth 2. Constructs not yet measured on this function: a `for` loop with the walk's test in the middle clause, a `switch`-dispatched loop back-edge, nested real loops (an outer once-through `for` around the walk), and `continue`-based back edges. Each is honest C with real semantics, unlike a wrapper device.

The honest expected outcome is that none beats 13 (H1/F5/F7 bound the score regardless) and the only movement available is on F4b's device weight — so this is a cheap cosmetic probe, NOT a reason to keep the function out of escalation.
